newsitem.title: USA: Accused spy for South Korea ordered held in jail.
newsitem.headline: Accused spy for South Korea ordered held in jail.

text.p: A federal judge on Wednesday ordered that U.S. Navy computer specialist Robert Kim, accused of passing secret documents to South Korea, be kept in jail pending his trial for espionage.
U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema granted the request by U.S. government prosecutors, overturning an earlier ruling by a magistrate that Kim be released on a $200,000 bond while he awaits trial.
"At this point, the evidence appears overwhelming," the judge said, adding that the likelihood of conviction was "quite high," increasing the risk that Kim might try to flee the country.

Korean-born Kim, 56, an 18-year government employee who became a U.S. citizen in 1974, has been accused of passing more than 40 classified documents to a South Korean embassy official since May. He was arrested last week while attending a diplomatic reception.
Prosecutors said Kim met with South Korean officials in March at a Washington-area hotel and discussed the possibility of working for Seoul after retiring from his post at U.S. Navy intelligence.
Brinkema said a transcript of that meeting, which was secretly taped by U.S. investigators, showed that Kim was trying to exploit his current position "to curry favour with South Korean officials."
